annotation.title_clean: Assistant to the President and OSTP Director Michael Kratsios' Intervention in the U.N. Security Council's "Security Council meeting on artificial intelligence and international security"
annotation.title_en: Assistant to the President and OSTP Director Michael Kratsios' Intervention in the U.N. Security Council's "Security Council meeting on artificial intelligence and international security"
annotation.authors_or_issuer: United States Mission to the United Nations
annotation.venue: United States Mission to the United Nations website
annotation.summary_en: Statement by White House OSTP Director Michael Kratsios at a UN Security Council meeting on AI and international security. It rejects global AI governance structures, stresses national sovereignty, permissionless innovation and domestic capacity building, and promotes the US AI Exports Program for partner nations.
key_provisions_or_claims: US rejects any global governance scheme or global regulator for AI
Countries should preserve national sovereignty in governing emerging technologies (Carolina Principles)
International bodies should share best practices to build domestic capacity, not regulatory regimes
US Exports Program offers partners secure AI infrastructure and adoption tools
US has engaged frontier labs on testing and set up cybersecurity clearinghouses
